rationale: Capacity is re-derived to six 56-card title parts (336 cards + README + index = 338 files), the smallest part count that keeps the measured 193 cards and 4 parts below the 80% warning and one measured peak day (25 cards) below the 90% rollover. The aggregates become the file bound times the per-file bound: a collection that may never be deleted or rolled over (ADR 0026) must never refuse a corpus whose every card is legal, and the 10,000-line total could (ADR 0029).

The generated projection gains the two title parts the re-derived 336-card capacity needs; cards_per_part stays at ADR 0022's 56 and every per-file bound is unchanged, so a full part is still 63 of 80 health lines. Both aggregate bands become files times the same band's per-file bound, so the projection can never fail on a total while each rendered part is healthy.

Measured at 30 of 32 files (93.8%, in rollover) with a peak of nine records in one active day, so the same law gives 44 files: 30 stays below the 80% warning and 30+9 below the 90% rollover. Aggregates become 44 times the unchanged per-file bounds; records are canonical and are never deleted, so a tighter total would be a stop with no legal exit (ADR 0029).

The question projection was already over its aggregate byte health target (267,938 of 262,144) and its 393,216-byte ceiling could not hold the re-derived 379-fact plane. File count and every per-file bound are unchanged; the aggregates become the closed topology's own arithmetic - the landing bound plus 32 shards at the shard bound - so they can never bind before it.
